name: Animated SOG (.asog) – streamable 4D Gaussian splat format
summary: Open file format and toolkit for 4D Gaussian splats (volumetric video in the browser). One .asog file holds moving splats with spherical harmonics and optional sound; repo ships the v1 spec, a Python encoder/decoder + flip-book pipeline, and PlayCanvas and three.js players. Example from the README: 180 per-frame PLY scans (3.6 GB) become one 12.4 MB file.

access.notes: Flip-book conversion needs a CUDA GPU and the external Open4DGS trainer (AGPL-3.0, not included). Sample Rubloff clips come from the Infinite-Realities Datasets (cite as requested). Not yet on PyPI/npm: install from the repo.

procedure: Open https://github.com/arrival-space/animated-sog or try the browser viewers (PlayCanvas / three.js links in the README).
Download the repo (Code > Download ZIP) or git clone it.
Install the Python package from the repo's python/ folder, then run `asog encode clip.trigsbin clip.asog --audio sound.mp3` on a TRiGS clip exported by Open4DGS.
For a folder of per-frame 3DGS PLYs, run `asog flipbook run frames/ work/` (CUDA GPU + Open4DGS required, see docs/pipeline.md).
Play the file with AsogPlayer (PlayCanvas) or AsogThreePlayer (three.js) from the js/ package; sample clips are in test-data/.

verdict.why: Real, MIT-licensed format + encoder + two web players for streaming 4D splat clips with sound; README backs the size claims (3.6 GB to 12.4 MB). Useful for volumetric-video creators on the web. Young (format v1, 47 stars), encoding depends on external AGPL Open4DGS.

image.alt: Animated 4D Gaussian splat of a man standing and gesturing, played from a single .asog file
